title: fix(service-queue): reclaim a running job whose lease ran out, and renew a live handler's lease
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgC5DLD798CXXfMJSTLB6VJi)_

domain:server#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CYVV6fcAQrNTDQRvPb

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：数据库队列在处理器还没跑完时进程挂了（崩溃、OOM、重新部署），那条任务现在会在租约到期后被下一次轮询收回：记一次失败尝试，按退避重排，次数用尽进死信；活着的慢处理器会定期续租，不会被别的节点抢走重跑。
- 为什么改：`leaseMs` 文档写着"到期后可由其他 worker 回收"，但认领只读 `pending`，挂掉的任务永远停在 `running`，既不重试也不进死信，运维看不到。
- 风险与回滚：多节点（未开 soleWriter）时每个租约窗口（默认 30 秒）多一条带索引的读，空闲一小时从 125 条变 246 条；单写者（soleWriter，云端租户内核）只在开机多读一次，空闲一小时不再多读。处理器若同步阻塞事件循环超过大半个租约，会被当成死掉而重跑。回滚即撤本 PR，无数据迁移。
- 先看：`packages/services/service-queue/src/db-queue-adapter.ts` 的 `reclaimRow`（CAS 谓词）、`renewLease`（续租）、`reclaimExpired`（读的节流界）与 `nextDueAt`（并入最早活租约）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-queue exec vitest run src/db-queue-idle-backoff.test.ts -t 30228`，预期 9 条全绿；其中"CRASHED-WORKER FIXTURE"一条在修复前的代码上是红的。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

Fixes #30228

Clause-②: no — restores the documented `leaseMs` reclaim; no accept set or export widens
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changes

The card's acceptance, quoted:

> 1. A `running` row whose `locked_until` has passed is claimable again (or moved to the retry path with its attempt counted), within one idle tick of the lease running out.
> 2. A live worker that is still inside its lease is never double-claimed.
> 3. Pins: a crashed-worker fixture (row left `running` with an expired lease) is reclaimed; a row inside its lease is not. The `nextDueAt` read #29919 adds (PR #30225) also counts the earliest lease expiry, so a sole-writer loop wakes for it.

**Reclaim (item 1).** `pollOnce()` now starts with `reclaimExpired()`: one read of the table's `status = 'running'` rows ordered by `locked_until`, every queue's (reclaiming runs nothing, so a row of a queue this node does not subscribe to just goes back to `pending` for whoever does; the predicate is the claim read's plain `status` equality, served by the declared `status` index, with no operator a stand-in engine might not answer), and each row whose lease has passed (or that has no lease at all) goes to the retry path. Of the card's two options this takes the second, retry path with the attempt counted, because `attempts` is written only after a handler settles: a worker that died left the row one attempt short, so reclaiming without counting would retry forever a message that kills its worker every time (an OOM on a large payload). The reclaim writes that attempt down and takes the branch a thrown handler takes: `pending` on its backoff, or `dlq` once `max_attempts` is spent, with `last_error` naming the dead worker. A reclaimed row counts in the tick's result, so the loop snaps back to `pollIntervalMs` and claims it on its backoff rather than after the idle ceiling.

**The reclaim write is a compare-and-set (item 2).** Its predicate re-states the expiry: `id`, `status: 'running'`, the `locked_by` it read, and `locked_until` null or at most now. A holder that renewed between the read and the write matches nothing and keeps its run. It is a `multi: true` write on purpose: the by-id path binds only the primary key and drops the rest of the predicate (the `outbox-dispatcher-scope.ts` precedent). Two workers reclaiming the same row write the same values from the same read and neither runs it, so that race costs nothing. `sys_job_queue` carries no tenant column (ADR-0131 D7), so the predicate writes need no tenant-audit warrant.

**A live handler renews its lease (item 2).** This is the risk the reclaim itself introduces. Before, nothing reclaimed, so a handler slower than `leaseMs` was safe; with a reclaim and no renewal it would be reclaimed mid-run and run twice. `dispatch()` now moves its row's `locked_until` a full window ahead every third of `leaseMs` while the handler runs: a `multi: true` compare-and-set on `locked_by = workerId`, logged when it matches nothing (the lease was lost underneath). A lease therefore passes only when its holder stopped renewing: the process died, or its event loop was blocked for most of a window. That is how a dead worker is told apart from a slow one, and the `leaseMs` doc now says the one thing an author must know: keep synchronous stretches well under the lease.

**The read is bounded, not per tick.** The read also returns the earliest lease still running. No lease can run out before the earlier of that lease and `now + leaseMs` (every running row was in the read, a row claimed after it holds at least `leaseMs` from its claim, and renewal only moves a lease later), so the next read waits until then. A full page means more may be hidden, so the next tick reads again. Cost without `soleWriter`: a busy 1 s poll pays one reclaim read per lease window; an idle loop at the 30 s ceiling pays one per tick, and an idle hour at the defaults goes from 125 to 246 reads (pinned).

**A sole writer reads once per boot.** With `soleWriter` no other process claims rows, so the window term is dropped. The first read after `start` finds what a crashed previous process left behind; after it, the only leases that can run out are the live ones it saw and this process's own claims whose settling write (completed, retry, dead letter, release) failed and left the row `running`. The adapter keeps those unsettled claims' leases (renewal moves them, a settling write drops them, the next read replaces them all), reads again only when one runs out, and folds them into `nextDueAt`. An idle sole writer's hour carries one reclaim read, the boot's, against 120 for the same hour without the flag (pinned); its fresh first minute goes from 2 to 3 reads.

**`nextDueAt` counts the earliest live lease (item 3).** Built on #30225's `DbQueueAdapter.nextDueAt` after it merged (771b2db20). The reclaim read already returns the earliest lease still running; the adapter keeps it, and `nextDueAt` answers the earliest of that, a sole writer's unsettled claims and the earliest deferred `scheduled_for`, at no read of its own. That read ran on the empty tick the answer follows, or the bound it set has not passed. A `soleWriter` loop, which otherwise sleeps to its ceiling, now wakes when a row its own previous process left `running` across a restart runs out of lease. The window term (`now + leaseMs`) is deliberately not in the answer: it only bounds the next read, and folding it in would wake a sole-writer loop every lease window for nothing.

**Docs.** Read sentence by sentence, none made false by this PR, left unchanged: `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx:287` ("multi-node claim via a lease on the `db` adapter", note 6648413565) is now true as written; `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`, the `dispatchSoleWriter` / `db.soleWriter` paragraph and the idle-cost sentences, describe the HTTP and notification dispatchers' reads and the flag's meaning, both still exact (the queue's sole-writer loop still sleeps to its next due time or the ceiling; a lease is one more due time); `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/audit-service.mdx:71`'s `locked_until` is the account lock's field on an auth audit event, not the queue's; the package README's `leaseMs` line is now true.

## Tests

`packages/services/service-queue/src/db-queue-idle-backoff.test.ts`, new `#30228` block, on that file's counting engine (its `update` already opens with `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`; it now applies a `multi` dispatch to the rows its `where` matches and reports the count):

- **CRASHED-WORKER FIXTURE**: a row written `running`, `locked_by: 'worker_dead'`, lease 1 ms past: one tick returns it to `pending`, `attempts: 1`, `scheduled_for` = now + 1 s, `last_error` naming the worker; on its backoff it runs as attempt 2 and completes.
- A lease that runs out while the loop is deep in its idle backoff (another node's crash, nothing tells this process) is reclaimed within one idle interval of expiry and run.
- The lost run counts: a fixture at `attempts: 2` of 3 goes to `dlq`, and `listFailed` returns it.
- A row inside its lease is not touched (no write at all).
- CAS: a renewal landing between the reclaim read and its write leaves the row `running` under its holder.
- A live handler three leases long, with a second adapter polling the same table: one run, `completed`, `attempts: 1`.
- In #29919's block: a sole-writer adapter booting over a row its previous process left `running`, lease 40 s from expiry, ceiling 5 min: the row runs at exactly 41 s (reclaimed at the lease's expiry, then its 1 s backoff).
- A sole writer's idle hour, with one job run at 10 min, makes exactly 1 reclaim read; the same hour without `soleWriter` makes 120 (the engine counts the reclaim read on its own).
- A sole writer whose `completed` write fails once (the row stays `running` under itself) reclaims it when its 3 s lease runs out and runs it again: 2 runs, `completed`, `attempts: 2`, 2 reclaim reads (boot, then the expired lease).

Moved pins in the same file, each with its reason in the comment: the idle hour (125 → 125 + 121), the flat-poll negative control (3602 → 3602 + 121), the per-tick cost (n claim reads + 1 reclaim read, then n on a tick inside the same window), the sole-writer fresh minute (2 → 3) and its ramping control (6 → 6 + 2).

The six reclaim legs, run against the pre-fix adapter before the `origin/main` merge (`db-queue-adapter.ts` restored from the branch base `6f095b9c`, blob `67be673a`, then restored to HEAD and proved byte-identical). The seventh leg (sole-writer restart) needs #30225's loop; its before-reading is ablation A4 below.

```
before  × CRASHED-WORKER FIXTURE: an expired lease goes back to the retry path …   AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
        × a lease that runs out while the loop is deep in its idle backoff …       row still { status: 'running', attempts: 0 }
        × the lost run counts: … dead-lettered, not retried forever                AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
        ✓ a row INSIDE its lease is never reclaimed                                (trivially: nothing reclaimed anything)
        ✓ the reclaim is a compare-and-set …                                       (trivially)
        ✓ a LIVE handler three leases long is never double-claimed …               (trivially)
after   ✓ all of them, and the whole package: Test Files 5 passed (5), Tests 91 passed (91)
```

</details>

| Leg | Mutation | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | `renewLease` replaced by a no-op | live handler reclaimed and run twice | red: `expected [ 'a', 'b' ] to deeply equal [ 'a' ]` |
| A2 | the expired-lease term deleted from the reclaim predicate | CAS leg red | red: `expected 1 to be +0` (a renewed lease was taken back) |
| A3 | the `now + leaseMs` window bound dropped | a lease another node takes after the read is never re-read | red: idle-reclaim leg, plus both cost pins (measured before the merge: 3602 and 125 reads against the then pins 3722 and 245) |
| A4 | the live lease dropped from `nextDueAt` | sole-writer restart leg red | red: `expected [] to have a length of 1` (no run inside the minute) |

A1–A6 were re-run on head `8d430e0c` (A3 now also reds the sole-writer and ramp-control pins, 5 legs in all).

A0 (the whole pre-fix adapter) is the before/after above. Each leg's on-disk landing and restore are printed by the tool (`anchor 1 -> 0`, `blob == HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty).

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The pending → running claim is still the by-id write it was (the comment above it says so: concurrent claimers may both take a `pending` row, and delivery is at-least-once). This PR does not change that; it adds no new way to double-claim, and the reclaim never runs anything itself.
- A worker whose lease was reclaimed while it was stalled and then finishes still writes its terminal state by id. The renewal logs the lost lease; making the terminal writes a compare-and-set on `locked_by` too would close that last window and is a separate change.
- Deviation: `census +2 write sites (reclaimRow, renewLease), surface widened by seat 03:38Z`. `check:tenant-audit-census` counts every engine write call site, so `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md` are regenerated (`node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`) and the page's hand-written figures moved with them (259 → 261 sites, 182 → 184 decidable, 107 → 109 undecidable, 66 → 68 const-named, 56% → 55%).
- Leases assume every node runs the same `leaseMs`, as they do when the nodes share one `QueueServicePlugin` configuration. A node with a shorter lease than this one's is still reclaimed, at most one lease window late.
